name: SkyShield (WMPGang)
tagline: A physically based 3D orrery that puts near-Earth objects and meteoroid streams in one view to show the overlooked hazard to satellites.
problem: Asteroid-risk tools focus on large near-Earth objects, while the steady flux of small meteoroids from streams and the sporadic complex is a constant, overlooked threat to satellites.
solution: A JavaScript/Three.js web orrery that computes orbits from orbital elements at their epoch: planets, dwarf planets, 1,669 NEOs from the ESA risk list, 107 meteoroid streams and the sporadic meteoroid complex. Streams light up only when active near Earth; NEOs filter by orbit, size and Palermo impact rating; time runs live, faster or backwards.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Won the award for the best and most valid use of science.
Identifies satellite risk zones using real-time data on near-Earth objects and meteor streams.
The team comes from a university meteor physics group and adds the meteoroid threat that NEO tools overlook.
Positions are computed from physical orbital elements at each object's epoch, so objects appear where they truly are at the chosen time.
Domain experts answering a visualization challenge with a physically correct model is what the science award rewards: the orrery is accurate, not just pretty.

lessons: Bring real domain expertise to a visualization challenge and let accuracy be the differentiator.
Add the hazard everyone ignores (meteoroids next to asteroids) to make a standard brief your own.
AI was used only for code snippets and debugging, and the disclosure says so.
